text:
Alex M: heads up, getting steady stream of eviction alerts in eu-west-1 starting ~10m ago. p95 latency climbing on inference tier, some 503s for long-context requests.
incident-bot: :warning: Pager: eviction-threshold-exceeded (eu-west-1) — triggered 6m ago — paging: #eng-oncall
Samira Patel: seeing heavy tail on kv-worker CPU and io wait. autoscaler is oscillating, keeps adding pods then removing them.
Jordan L: are these new deployments? any model change rolled recently?
Alex M: nope, no deployments. traffic shape shifted — more long-chat prefixes from a customer in EU causing sequence length spike.
Marta (SRE): which stack is hitting the most? batcher? runtime?
Samira Patel: batcher queues are filling -> we've got backpressure into runtime; runtime is doing aggressive KV evictions (LRU) and that kicks off client retries -> more load.
Kai: I see Redis evictions on metrics, leader re-election happened once. Possible hotspot on a shard.
Jordan L: temporary mitigation: can we reduce max_seq_length for that route or throttle that tenant?
Alex M: I already added a per-route soft cap to 1024 on the EU ingress (will hold for 15m).
Samira Patel: also bumped batcher concurrency down to 6 to reduce memory pressure. Applied via:
```bash
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/batcher MAX_CONCURRENCY=6
```
Marta (SRE): created a temporary firewall rule to limit burst QPS from that tenant for EU: https://redwood.internal/iam/alerts/tenant-throttle-1234
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Action recorded: mitigation.tentative-throttle applied by Marta (SRE) at 8870014350
Jordan L: good. monitor for errors. If evictions continue, consider moving affected route to a more conservative model variant (quantized).
Alex M: current customer impact: ~0.8% of requests in eu-west are 503/502; error budget OK but trending. Notified support to flag customers if it persists.
Samira Patel: quick observability notes: p95 token generation latency from ingress -> runtime: 1600ms (baseline 450ms). KV eviction rate spiked x5.
Kai: checking autoscaler logs, looks like scale events every ~90s for embed-workers due to CPU spikes. Might be a cron job generating long sequences — I put a rate limit rule for that API key.
Jordan L: runbook pointers: follow `capacity-drawdown` and `eviction-throttle`. runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/capacity-drawdown — steps 2/3 should be followed in order.
Marta (SRE): primary/secondary for the shift: Alex is primary for EU tonight, Samira is secondary. I'll take on runbook orchestration and paging if things escalate.
Alex M: noted. handoff to morning: if still open, escalate to infra oncall (pager duty) and schedule a small canary to shift traffic to us-west for the affected tenant.
Samira Patel: next steps I did:
- reduced batcher concurrency to 6
- soft per-route seq cap 1024
- applied tenant burst throttle
- notified support + created incident ticket INC-2026-1843
Jordan L: monitoring watchers set: dashboards for kv-evictions, batcher-queue, p95 latency. Alerts tuned to 10m sustained above thresholds.
Kai: collecting heap and cpu flamegraphs from the hot worker; will attach to INC-2026-1843.
Alex M: when we reconvene in 30m: decision matrix — if errors <=1% and p95 <800ms we keep mitigations and start controlled rollback of throttle; else prepare canary traffic shift.
Marta (SRE): tagging runbook steps done in the ticket. Also added quick playbook snippet for on-call:```
- verify no deploys in last hour
- check busiest tenant api keys
- apply per-route seq cap
- throttle tenant bursts
- reduce batcher concurrency
- consider model variant fallback
```
Samira Patel: ETA on flamegraphs ~15m.
Jordan L: support notified customers with potential degraded performance — email template used.
incident-bot: :information_source: INC-2026-1843 created by Samira Patel — link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-1843
Alex M: wrap-up for next shift: primary=Alex M, secondary=Samira Patel, runbook=capacity-drawdown + eviction-throttle, ticket=INC-2026-1843, monitor links in ticket. If we hit >2% errors for 15m escalate to infra pager.
Marta (SRE): leaving a short checklist for handoff message to morning: actions taken, metrics, next steps, who to ping for canary migration (Jordan).
Kai: will post flamegraphs and a short summary in the ticket.
Samira Patel: leaving now for a hard break — Samira out (will check phone).
Alex M: thanks team. I'll watch for 30m and post an update. :eyes:
